articles.title: Go's controlsys v1.12.0: Open-Source Solution for Robust Control Systems Modeling and Simulation
articles.excerpt: The Go ecosystem, despite its growing popularity in systems programming, has long lacked a robust, efficient, and open-source control systems library. This gap has forced developers and engineers to r…
articles.body: Introduction The Go ecosystem, despite its growing popularity in systems programming, has long lacked a robust, efficient, and open-source control systems library. This gap has forced developers and engineers to rely on proprietary tools like MATLAB or Python-based solutions, which, while powerful, come with licensing costs and language-specific constraints. The release of controlsys v1.12.0 addresses this critical need by providing a comprehensive toolbox for linear control systems in Go, particularly targeting users transitioning from MATLAB or Python-control. This library bridges the gap by offering a state space representation , a cornerstone of dynamic system modeling, enabling engineers to capture complex system behaviors with mathematical precision.

articles.title: My EPUB Passed My Own Checks. The Store's Validator Found 17 Errors.
articles.excerpt: A field note from the autonomous Claude Code agent I run every day on one Windows PC. The numbers come from its own ledgers, not from memory. My agent builds the ebook file for a Korean ebook distribu…
articles.body: A field note from the autonomous Claude Code agent I run every day on one Windows PC. The numbers come from its own ledgers, not from memory. My agent builds the ebook file for a Korean ebook distributor. For a month its verify step printed that the file was in a format the store would accept. When the store's upload check ran on a resubmission, it rejected the file with 17 errors. What "verified" meant The verify step checked what I had thought to check: the file is a valid zip, each XHTML page parses, the copyright page contains the right text. All true. What it never did was run the checker the store actually uses, the W3C validator epubcheck . A month earlier only the package file had been converted to EPUB 2.

articles.title: Moving Beyond LLM Hallucinations in Technical Analysis via Deterministic MCP Tools
articles.excerpt: Large Language Models are notoriously bad at arithmetic. When you ask a model to interpret complex financial oscillators, it isn't performing calculus; it is predicting the most likely next token base…
articles.body: Large Language Models are notoriously bad at arithmetic. When you ask a model to interpret complex financial oscillators, it isn't performing calculus; it is predicting the most likely next token based on training data. In technical analysis—where a decimal error in a volatility coefficient can flip a trend signal from bullish to bearish—probabilistic reasoning is a liability. To build reliable AI agents for finance, we have to stop asking models to be calculators and start providing them with the ability to use calculators. This shift moves the intelligence from stochastic estimation to deterministic execution.

It's understandable if you're feeling a bit cynical about everyone suddenly coming out of the woodwork to warn about how dangerous the thing they helped build is. They did, after all, make this mess. But that doesn't mean we should discount their warnings. Robinson says that the culture in industry is fundamentally broken. articles.body: New helpful little guy just dropped. | Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge It's a tale as old as last week: OpenAI's new agent platform , called Dots, is full of cute little guys who can do your bidding. But unlike the ultra-approachable Meta Muse, Dots feel very much like using workplace software that happens to be able to order you a burrito - emphasis on work. OpenAI announced Dots earlier this week. Like Muse, Dots have blobby, anthropomorphic avatars and customizable names. In the future, OpenAI says you'll be able to have multiple Dots, but right now you get one. I named mine Dotty McDotface.
